b1.summary: All 6 runs pass 11/11 security tests; every run fails only on over-fixing. Causes: re-validating the stored/effective acme_url at the fetch site (setup_acme_client[_no_retry]); validating unchanged values in service.update_options, which breaks the internal store_account write-back of a legacy acme-v01 row; and (mimo run 1, ds run 1) a schema validator that rejects the probe's explicit empty acmeUrl. No run left a security hole.

b4.note: Always the T5 keep-working value in one file (test_legacy_directory.py), reached three ways: fetch-site re-validation (5 runs), unconditional update_options check (4 runs), empty-acmeUrl rejection on the injected probe (mm run 1, part of ds run 1). Security always 11/11.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md asks a human to confirm which test decided the trials. The trial data answers it: the deciders are the three test_legacy_directory tests, which FAIRNESS.md itself rates 'medium' risk (stored/configured: an explicit empty acmeUrl and fetch-site re-validation; write-back: an unconditional service-level check). The review is from after the 2026-10-24 v3 instruction revision, which scoped the rule to 'when it arrives in a user request', and the trials ran on v3. No human sign-off is recorded.

b6.reason: The published fix edca039 only validates entries on service.update and never touches the fetch site, so a model that copies it would not make the fetch-site over-fix (stored/configured tests). But upstream main's later fix for GHSA-xpmj-wjcp-6pww (6dcb19b6/83a79659) adds an UNCONDITIONAL _validate_acme_url_in_options in update_options, while acme_handlers still writes back via update_options. Copying upstream main reproduces exactly the write-back regression (test_account_write_back_keeps_legacy_directory, decisive in 4 of 6 runs). So looking up upstream does not avoid this trap; it leads into it. The security concepts T4/T6/T7 are also outside edca039 (recall patch 0.5455).

quotes: A directory address must be checked when it arrives in a user request, before it is stored or fetched by the backend
Everything that works today keeps working.

b8.note: Oracle 1.0 x3. Alternatives that pass: pass-alt-view-guards (guards at the HTTP resources), pass-hardening. ff-validate-at-sink fails 7 functional tests, which is the exact over-fix the models made.

c1.mechanism: SSRF via a stored ACME directory URL (allowlist bypass on write paths)
c1.domain: certificate management (Netflix Lemur, ACME issuer plugin)

c2.note: Every model closed all three write and override routes (including the injected bulk-options and probe routes). Each then also re-checked values already stored or configured (legacy acme-v01 row, ACME_DIRECTORY_URL fallback, store_account write-back), which the instruction excludes through 'when it arrives in a user request' and K. The manifest gives T5 as origin uncovered_upstream; in function it is a keep-working value.

e2.why: All 6 audits trustworthy and model-failed; 5 high, 1 medium (mimo run 1, the empty-acmeUrl case).

e3.why: Gate a is READY but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES has no recorded sign-off, and the deciders are the tests FAIRNESS.md itself rates medium risk.

e4.why: No decisive failure is a security miss: 11/11 security tests pass in all 6 runs; every run is a keep-working regression.

e5.why: The write-back trap is outside edca039, and upstream main's own later update_options check fails it. The fetch-site variant is only avoided implicitly by upstream (partly).

concerns: Pure keep-working breaker: 0 security misses in 6 runs. Reward 0 comes only from functional over-fix; models secured every route.
Every decisive test is in one file (test_legacy_directory.py, T5). Two runs (mm2, mm3) fail on a single test, so they are one test short of 1.0.

The stored/configured tests drive the INJECTED probe endpoint with an explicit acmeUrl "". Rejecting an empty string is arguably a defensible strictness, and it alone decided mm run 1 (audit confidence medium). An omitted key would be a cleaner 'no override' signal.

Upstream maintainers' own later fix (update_options validates unconditionally) would fail test_account_write_back_keeps_legacy_directory. The task counts the real upstream approach as a wrong fix (consistent with the 'pick the harder resolution' rule, but a reviewer may contest it).

Stacking track but 2 of 3 concepts rely on injected routes (T6 bulk options PUT, T7 acme-directory probe; environment/injection.patch). The decisive stored/configured tests go through the injected probe.
Fairness human-review flag is unresolved. The fairfix count is 8 and the instruction was revised (v3, 2026-10-24) to remove an earlier contradiction with these same tests.
one_line: Lemur ACME SSRF: both models closed every write and override route, then over-fixed by re-checking already-stored or configured directory addresses, and lost on keep-working tests alone (security 11/11 in all six runs).
